channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: Red Hat Releases gnome-remote-desktop Security Update
item.description: A security update for gnome-remote-desktop on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 addresses multiple vulnerabilities that could allow remote code execution. The flaws, rated Important by Red Hat Product Security, carry CVSS scores that indicate high exploitation risk, though no active exploits have been reported.

item.title: Inception Gang Launches Large-Scale Vishing Campaign
item.description: Inception, a new extortion group, launched a large-scale vishing campaign targeting SSO credentials of global brands and firms. The campaign uses social engineering calls to harvest SSO tokens, potentially enabling unauthorized corporate account access; no encryption or exfiltration has been reported. Teams should enforce MFA, monitor login anomalies, and train staff on phishing to mitigate the threat.

item.title: Red Hat Issues openssl Security Patch
item.description: An OpenSSL security update for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.2 EUS addresses multiple cryptographic flaws that could enable downgrade attacks. The vulnerabilities, rated Moderate by Red Hat Product Security, have CVSS scores indicating moderate risk and no confirmed wild exploitation. Red Hat has issued the patch; users should update OpenSSL to the latest version to prevent potential downgrade exploits.

item.title: Erlang OTP Vulnerabilities Prompt Update
item.description: Erlang OTP multiple versions are affected by security flaws that could allow unauthorized code execution via the runtime system. The advisory, issued by the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, does not list specific CVE identifiers but notes a CVSS base score indicating moderate severity. Administrators should review the provided web link and apply any available updates to mitigate potential exploitation.

item.title: California Privacy Agency Director Kemp Resigns After Two Years
item.description: California Privacy Protection Agency director Charles Kemp announced his departure after a two-year tenure. His exit follows the launch of the agency’s first-in-the-nation platform that enables consumers to opt out of data sharing. The agency will continue to enforce privacy regulations and support consumer data rights under new effective leadership.

item.title: CVE-2026-135614 - Sensitive data redaction bypass in the troubleshooting tool in Amazon ECS MCP Server
item.description: Bulletin ID: 2026-200-AWS Publication Date: 11/24/2026 11:00 AM PST Description: Amazon ECS MCP Server is an open-source Model Context Protocol server that lets AI agents and assistants manage and troubleshoot Amazon ECS workloads using the operator's AWS credentials. We identified CVE-2026-135614, an issue in the troubleshooting tool of the Amazon ECS MCP Server (awslabs.ecs-mcp-server) before 0.1.36.

item.title: CVE-2026-135414 - Server-side request forgery in snapshot repository registration in Amazon OpenSearch Service
item.description: Bulletin ID: 2026-201-AWS Publication Date: 11/24/2026 11:15 AM PST Description: Amazon OpenSearch Service is a managed service for deploying, operating, and scaling OpenSearch clusters in the AWS Cloud. We identified CVE-2026-135414, an issue in snapshot repository registration in Amazon OpenSearch Service.

item.title: Turnitin Reports Unauthorized Activity on Customer Systems
item.description: Turnitin announced that it detected unauthorized activity involving certain customer-facing systems, according to a statement from CEO Chris Caren. The company did not disclose specific details or evidence of data compromise, but the incident indicates potential exploitation of exposed interfaces. Turnitin urged customers to review access controls, monitor logs, and apply any available security updates to mitigate the threat.

item.title: CVE-2026-134066 - Query injection via schema-derived identifiers in Graph Explorer
item.description: Bulletin ID: 2026-199-AWS Publication Date: 11/24/2026 10:30 AM PST Description: Graph Explorer is an open-source tool for browsing and searching graph data, which customers self-host against Amazon Neptune or other graph databases. We identified CVE-2026-134066, an issue in the query construction of Graph Explorer before version 3.2.1.

item.title: VMware vCenter Vulnerabilities Require Patch
item.description: VMware vCenter and Cloud Foundation versions before 9.1.2 and 9.0.2 contain vulnerabilities that could enable remote code execution. The advisory, issued by the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, references a CVSS base score but does not provide a CVE identifier, indicating moderate risk. VMware has released patches for affected products; administrators should apply the updates promptly to prevent potential exploitation.

item.title: Wiz Shares FedRAMP VDR & VER Insights
item.description: Wiz Research hosted a FedRAMP VDR & VER event on November 12, gathering government officials, industry experts, and its own FedRAMP team to discuss modernizing vulnerability management. The session highlighted new FedRAMP requirements, emphasizing automated vulnerability detection, continuous verification, and streamlined remediation workflows. Participants were urged to use Wiz’s platform for real-time compliance monitoring and align operations with FedRAMP.

item.title: Socket Provides Free Patches for All Critical RubyGems CVEs
item.description: Socket has released free patches that address every critical RubyGems vulnerability without requiring dependency upgrades. The patches cover all CVEs flagged as critical by the RubyGems security team, ensuring immediate remediation for affected projects. Security teams should download the patches from Socket’s repository and apply them via the provided installation scripts or package managers.

item.title: Chrome for Android Update
item.description: We've just released Chrome 159 (159.0.8154.33) for Android to a small percentage of users. It'll become available on Google Play over the next few days. If you find a new issue, please let us know by filing a bug .

item.title: AWS pgactive Buffer Overflow Enables Authenticated RCE
item.description: A stack-based buffer overflow in AWS pgactive’s replication origin name parsing lets an authenticated database user with specific privileges run arbitrary OS commands. The flaw, CVE-2026-134068, permits privilege-escalated code execution on the database host, threatening the entire PostgreSQL cluster. AWS has issued a patch for all affected versions (≥ 2.1.0); administrators should apply it immediately to close the RCE vector.

item.title: Radware Breach Exposes Customer Cloud Access Keys
item.description: Radware reported that attackers accessed customer account details and cloud access keys via an unsecured internal Cloud WAF management API left exposed online. The exposed API permitted retrieval of credentials that could be used to compromise customer cloud environments. Radware has disclosed the breach; affected customers should review logs and rotate keys.

item.title: Lawmakers Urge ID Verification Firms to Strengthen Security
item.description: Lawmakers issued a bipartisan letter urging identity verification firms to strengthen security following the September data breach at IDscan. The letter highlights ongoing vulnerabilities in ID verification services and calls for enhanced safeguards to protect user data. Industry stakeholders should review compliance frameworks and implement robust controls to mitigate future breaches.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Important Update for resource-agents
item.description: Red Hat released an Important security update for the resource-agents package on Enterprise Linux 8, addressing multiple vulnerabilities that could affect cluster resource management. The advisory references CVSS base scores for each flaw, indicating high-severity risks that could lead to unauthorized access or denial of service within the cluster. Administrators should apply the update immediately to mitigate the identified weaknesses.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical Fence-Agents Update
item.description: Red Hat released a critical security update for fence-agents on RHEL 8, fixing vulnerabilities that could let local attackers gain elevated privileges. The advisory cites CVSS base scores for each flaw, indicating high severity, though specific CVE IDs are not listed. Red Hat urges immediate installation of the updated fence-agents package to prevent privilege escalation and potential code execution.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102942: Important: mariadb:11.8 security update
item.description: An update for the mariadb:11.8 module is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 Extended Update Support. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Volant Manticore Deploys IPFS-Based KuboShell Backdoor
item.description: Iran-aligned Volant Manticore has targeted telecommunications firms, airlines, and critical infrastructure in Cyprus, using a custom backdoor named KuboShell. KuboShell leverages the InterPlanetary File System for command-and-control and deploys the Homa post-compromise framework, enabling stealthy persistence. Security teams should monitor for IPFS traffic, block known KuboShell signatures, and apply network segmentation to mitigate potential espionage.

item.title: Tanium Vulnerabilities Span Multiple Product Versions
item.description: Tanium disclosed vulnerabilities in Core Content, Enhanced Tags, Default Content, Endpoint Configuration Toolset, Engage, Zone Server, and Threat Response across multiple versions. Flaws enable local privilege escalation or arbitrary code execution, with CVSS scores 6.5-8.3, but no active exploitation reported. Apply the latest patches or upgrade to the minimum recommended versions to mitigate the risks.

item.title: VMware Patches Critical ESX and vCenter Vulnerabilities
item.description: VMware disclosed a critical authentication bypass in vCenter and code execution flaws on ESX hosts, identified by CVE-2026-123903. The flaw permits unauthenticated attackers to gain control of vCenter and run arbitrary code on ESX servers, threatening virtual infrastructure. VMware issued an out-of-band patch; administrators should apply it immediately to secure affected systems.

item.title: ShinyHunters claims to return after FBI arrests, uses old PGP keys as proof
item.description: The ShinyHunters extortion gang claims to have returned in posts on a new data leak site after a series of arrests over the past two months targeting alleged members.

item.title: EU Academy Breach Stole User Data
item.description: The European Commission confirmed attackers breached its EU Academy learning hub and stole personal data of an undisclosed number of users. The breach exposed user credentials and demographic details, enabling potential identity theft or phishing attacks against EU staff and students. The Commission must investigate, notify affected users, and reinforce access controls on the EU Academy platform.

item.title: Check Point Servers Compromised in 22-Org Campaign
item.description: Threat actors exploited multiple vulnerabilities to compromise Check Point Security management servers in an ongoing campaign that affected 22 organizations. The exploitation enabled attackers to gain administrative control over the servers, potentially exposing configuration data and internal network traffic. Check Point has released patches for the affected vulnerabilities; administrators should apply updates and review server hardening configurations.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102931: Important: grafana security update
item.description: An update for grafana is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: Microsoft Office Visio RCE CVE-2026-112732 Omitted
item.description: Microsoft Office Visio contains a remote code execution flaw identified as CVE-2026-112732, affecting all supported Visio versions. The flaw permits arbitrary code execution via crafted input, but no exploitation has been reported, and it was omitted from the November 2026 Security Updates. Microsoft released the patch in November 2026, and customers who installed those updates need not take further action.

item.title: Carnegie Endowment Donor Data Leaked by Vendor
item.description: The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace reported that a third-party vendor, Soapbox Engage, suffered a breach that leaked donor information. The leak exposed personal and financial details of donors, potentially enabling targeted phishing or identity theft campaigns. The Endowment should investigate the vendor’s security posture, notify affected donors, and enforce stricter data protection controls.

item.title: Red Hat Issues kernel-rt Update for RHEL 9.2 SAP
item.description: A kernel-rt security update fixes multiple privilege escalation and denial-of-service flaws in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.2 for SAP Solutions. Each vulnerability carries a CVSS score between 7.5 and 8.3, exposing local users to potential real-time scheduling disruption. Red Hat has issued the patch for all affected RHEL 9.

item.title: McDonald’s Japan Customer Data Breach Confirmed
item.description: McDonald’s Japan confirmed a breach where a third party accessed customer data stored behind its official mobile app. The exposed records included purchase histories, internal customer IDs, IP addresses, and mobile device location data, potentially compromising user privacy. McDonald’s Japan urged affected customers to monitor accounts and advised security teams to review access controls and data handling practices.

item.title: AI Development Adds Vulnerability Noise, Calls for Resilience
item.description: AI-driven development increases software supply-chain complexity, flooding security teams with low-risk vulnerabilities. RapidFort argues that runtime visibility, container hardening, and automated remediation can filter noise, reducing false positives and focusing resources on real threats. Security teams should adopt these practices to improve resilience, though no specific patch or CVE is cited.

item.title: Autonomous AI Agents Automate Multi-Platform Intrusions
item.description: Unit 42 tracked cyber campaigns featuring autonomous AI agents deployed to conduct multi-platform intrusions. Threat actors used these agentic systems to automate complex attacks using standard administrative tools while generating distinct operational traces. Security operations teams must monitor environment-specific telemetry to identify automated agent behaviors and mitigate multi-platform intrusion risks.

item.title: CISA Alerts on Exploited N-Able Email Bug
item.description: CISA warns that a vulnerability in N-Able’s email security platform has been exploited, threatening government departments. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-134624, allows attackers to bypass spam and malware filtering, potentially delivering malicious content to users. N-Able has released a patch; agencies must update before Thanksgiving to mitigate the critical risk.

item.title: EU Academy Data Exposed in AI-Assisted Attack
item.description: The European Commission discovered that an AI-assisted cyberattack exposed names and email addresses of EU Academy users. The breach, identified during an October investigation, indicates attackers accessed user data stored in the Academy’s systems, though no financial or credential theft was reported. The Commission is reviewing access controls and advising affected users to monitor for phishing attempts.

item.title: Chrome Vulnerability Affects Versions Before 158.0.8127.88
item.description: Google issued a security advisory for a vulnerability affecting Chrome versions prior to 158.0.8127.88 on Windows/Mac and 158.0.8127.88 on Linux. The flaw could allow attackers to compromise user sessions or execute code, though no exploitation reports are cited. Users and administrators should update to the latest Chrome release or apply the vendor’s patch as soon as it becomes available.

item.title: Cloudera Announces Sovereign AI Solution for Enterprise Environments
item.description: Cloudera launched Cloudera for Digital Sovereignty to provide enterprise technical and operational control across cloud, data, and AI lifecycles. The architecture combines Cloudera Anywhere Cloud with open-weight models to support deployments across sovereign clouds, private data centers, and air-gapped environments. Security teams can leverage open standards to maintain governed data pipelines while mitigating vendor lock-in risks.

item.title: n8n Vulnerabilities Affect Multiple Versions
item.description: n8n disclosed flaws in versions prior to 3.4.0, 2.50.0, 2.49.5, 2.48.8, 1.123.101, 2.49.4, 2.48.7, and 1.123.100. The flaws allow local privilege escalation or arbitrary code execution, with CVSS scores 6.0-8.0, but no active exploitation observed. Apply the latest patches or upgrade to the minimum recommended versions to mitigate the risks.

item.title: Astelia Introduces Autonomous Network Mitigation
item.description: Astelia released autonomous network mitigation that blocks attack paths to reachable vulnerabilities before patches are applied. The solution uses Frontier AI models to cut exploit time to near zero, covering the 1% of vulnerabilities attackers can reach without patching. Deploying the mitigation workflow requires six steps and a single approval branch, enabling organizations to prevent exploitation while awaiting vendor fixes.

item.title: Check Point Security Management Servers Targeted in Global Attacks
item.description: Threat actors compromised Check Point Security Management Servers across multiple international organizations using an AI-assisted campaign. Attackers initiated the intrusions from 99 distinct IP addresses to target enterprise networks across various global industry sectors. Network administrators must inspect management server logs for indicators of compromise associated with the identified infrastructure and isolate impacted management nodes.

item.title: Volant Manticore: Flying Under the Radar
item.description: Key Points Introduction Check Point Research is tracking a previously undocumented Iran-nexus threat group who we named Volant Manticore. What started in July 2026 as a single backdoor delivered to a Cyprus-based airline through a fake CV has since expanded into a broader cluster of activity that we traced back to September 2025.

item.title: Critical VMware ESX Flaws Let Remote Attackers Execute Malicious Code on Virtualization Hosts
item.description: Broadcom has disclosed 23 VMware vulnerabilities, including two critical flaws that could let attackers run code directly on ESX hosts and a third that could let them access vCenter without signing in. The Broadcom security advisory, VMSA-2026-0011, was published on November 24. It says the flaws were privately reported and does not report active exploitation.

item.title: McDonald's Japan Exposes App User Location Data
item.description: A data breach at McDonald's Japan exposed a database of official smartphone app users, revealing their location information. Attackers accessed the database through an undisclosed vulnerability, compromising personal data for thousands of customers without evidence of credential theft. McDonald's Japan has notified affected users and is working with security teams to investigate the breach and strengthen database access controls.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102938: Important: fltk security update
item.description: An update for fltk is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.2 Update Services for SAP Solutions. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: RHSA-2026:102859: Important: python3.12 security update
item.description: An update for python3.12 is now available for Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.4 Update Services for SAP Solutions. Red Hat Product Security has rated this update as having a security impact of Important. A Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) base score, which gives a detailed severity rating, is available for each vulnerability from the CVE link(s) in the References section.

item.title: UK NCSC Reports Rise in AI-Driven Cyber Attacks
item.description: Britain's National Cyber Security Centre reported a marked rise in artificial intelligence-assisted cyberattacks since September. NCSC advisories indicate that AI integration has significantly accelerated threat actor speed, operational scale, and persistence during network intrusion attempts. Defense teams must adapt detection strategies to identify high-velocity automated threats and enhance response capabilities against rapid attack lifecycles.

item.title: Red Hat Releases kernel Update for RHEL 9.4 SAP
item.description: A kernel security update addresses several privilege escalation and denial-of-service vulnerabilities in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.4 for SAP Solutions. The flaws have CVSS scores ranging from 7.0 to 8.2, allowing local users to potentially disrupt system operations. Red Hat has released the patch for all affected RHEL 9.4 SAP nodes; administrators should apply it immediately to mitigate the risks.

item.title: GTA 6 Hacker Sentenced, Released Same Day
item.description: A former Lapsus$ member, Arion Kurtaj, was sentenced to seven years for leaking Grand Theft Auto VI footage after a guilty plea. The case involved fraud and computer misuse charges, including unauthorized disclosure of proprietary game content in London. Court granted license release the same day; no further remediation required.

item.title: Hackers Deploy ZQAgent Backdoor to Run Malicious Commands and Access Files on Linux Servers
item.description: A new Linux backdoor called ZQAgent is giving attackers a long-term foothold on compromised servers. It can run commands, move through folders, read files and open network tunnels. The malware was dropped by ARTEX, an AI-driven hacking framework.

item.title: Shirudo AI Tool Protects Unpatched Linux Systems
item.description: OpenAI and Cisco released Shirudo, an open-source Linux security tool that deploys temporary runtime protections to block exploitation of unpatched vulnerabilities. Shirudo leverages AI-driven heuristics to detect and mitigate exploitation attempts against known CVEs without requiring service restarts, addressing the gap before patch deployment. Administrators can deploy Shirudo immediately to shield systems, then apply official patches once available.

item.title: Red Hat Issues kernel Update for RHEL 9 SAP
item.description: A kernel security update fixes multiple privilege escalation and denial-of-service flaws in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9. The vulnerabilities carry CVSS scores between 7.2 and 8.0, exposing local users to potential system disruption. Red Hat has issued the patch for all affected RHEL 9 nodes; administrators should apply it promptly to close the gaps.
